Every PR waited in the same queue, for the same few senior engineers. A renamed variable and a rewritten payment flow got the same amount of attention.

Seniors became the bottleneck. They skimmed. Risky changes slipped through.

Today we are launching LiveReview: a risk-aware code review system built to fix exactly that.

results.title: Introducing LiveReview: World’s First Generally Available Risk-Aware Code Review System
results.content:
Here’s how the loop works:

1.   Track outcomes. Trace production incidents and rollbacks back to the commits and reviews behind them.
2.   Learn from the data. Combine those outcomes with LLM analysis, static checks, and ML signals into one risk score per change.
3.   Automate selectively. Auto-approve the lowest-risk 30–50% of changes. Pick a conservative, balanced, or aggressive policy. Risky or uncertain changes still go to a human.
4.   Keep improving. Track incidents, false approvals, and overrides. Then tighten or loosen the policy as real data comes in.

The result? Your reviewers stop reading every line of every diff. Instead, they give their full attention to the 50–70% of changes that actually carry risk.

## Risk inside the diff, not just per PR [...] LiveReview follows the approach behind Meta’s internal AI review system, RADAR. The idea is simple: score every change for risk, fast-track the safe ones, and route the risky ones to the right reviewers.

At Meta, this approach led to:

   50× fewer production incidents
   3× fewer rollbacks
   35% faster reviews

LiveReview brings the same idea to any team, on any git provider. Self-hosted, and free.

## How LiveReview scores risk

Every pull request gets one risk score, built from three signals: [...] Most alternatives find issues and leave the approval decision to a person.

LiveReview makes the “does a human need to look at this?” call itself. It backs that call with your own production data. Only then does it prioritize what’s left for your reviewers.

You can see every row in the full feature-by-feature comparison.

## The real problem: reviews didn’t scale with AI

Most AI code review tools just add more comments to your pull request. But more comments was never the goal.

The real goals are fewer incidents, fewer rollbacks, and less senior reviewer time. That’s why we measure LiveReview by production outcomes, not comment count.

results.content:
LiveReview is a risk-aware AI code review system from Hexmos that scores every pull request and auto-approves the safest 30–50% without human review. It is free to start, self-hostable, and works across GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Gitea, and Azure DevOps.

## How does LiveReview decide which pull requests are safe to auto-approve?

Every pull request gets one risk score from three signals: semantic LLM analysis of what the change does, a custom ML model trained on your own incidents, rollbacks, and overrides, and static graph analysis of how far the change reaches. The blend is documented in the open repository and explained step by step in this founder deep dive. [...] Try ChatGate

# LiveReview: Free, Risk-Aware Code Review: Auto Approve Low-Risk Changes

Most AI review tools flag issues. LiveReview promises production results: fewer incidents, fewer rollbacks, less senior reviewer load. Every PR is risk-scored. The lowest-risk 30-50% are safely auto-approved; the risky ones go straight to the engineers who should see them. The approach is inspired by Meta's highly successful internal AI review system, where production incidents fell 50x and rollbacks 3x. LLM + incident-trained ML + code-graph analysis. Free and self-hostable.

Visit official site↗

LiveReview: Free, Risk-Aware Code Review: Auto Approve Low-Risk Changes [...] Self-hosting suits teams that want code on their own network, including fully local inference via Ollama; only the diff is sent to the model, and code is never stored or used for training. The limits are honest: risky or uncertain changes still need humans, the incident-trained model improves only once fed real outcomes, and production self-hosting needs Docker plus a reverse proxy. In short, LiveReview trades comment volume for fewer incidents and focused senior review. Explore it on the official site and compare notes on its live Product Hunt launch.
